cues.en: Where does math come from and what does it mean?
cues.zh: 數學從哪裡來，又代表什麼？

cues.en: Does math reveal the deepest, darkest secrets of the universe?
cues.zh: 數學揭露了宇宙最深層、最隱密的祕密嗎？

cues.en: Or is it simply a useful way to describe events in the world that some clever humans have thought up?
cues.zh: 還是只是一些聰明人想出來、描述世間事件的有用方法？

cues.en: In other words, has math always existed?
cues.zh: 換句話說，數學一直都存在，

cues.en: And we have discovered some fundamental laws of nature?
cues.zh: 而我們只是發現某些根本自然法則嗎？

cues.en: Or is math an imperfect language that humans have created?
cues.zh: 還是數學是人類創造的一種不完美語言？

cues.en: This debate is as old as mathematics itself, and well, it's not going to be answered any time soon.
cues.zh: 這個辯論和數學本身一樣古老，而且不會很快有答案。

cues.en: Certainly not in this video.
cues.zh: 這支影片肯定也不會。

cues.en: Instead, what I want to do in this video is introduce this debate and the dominant positions that people can take.
cues.zh: 我想做的，是介紹這個辯論，以及人們可能採取的主要立場。

cues.en: And I think this discussion is really interesting and it's worth taking a few minutes to introduce you to the topic.
cues.zh: 我覺得這個討論很有趣，值得花幾分鐘介紹。

cues.en: Now, before I start, let me state that there is zero doubt that math is indescribably important and useful.
cues.zh: 開始之前，先說明：數學極其重要而且有用，這完全沒有疑問。

cues.en: Math is central to progress in basically every technological development, from communications to transportation to medicine to entertainment.
cues.zh: 從通訊、交通、醫療到娛樂，基本上每項科技發展的進步，都以數學為核心。

cues.en: So this debate is not about whether math is useful or not.
cues.zh: 所以不是在辯論數學有沒有用。

cues.en: Instead, it's more of a philosophical debate about whether math exists in the universe without humans
cues.zh: 而是更哲學性的問題：即使沒有人類

cues.en: to write it down, just like gravity or planets exist in the universe, or whether math is something that we created.
cues.zh: 把數學寫下來，它是否也像重力或行星一樣存在於宇宙，還是我們創造了數學？

cues.en: And, you know, it doesn't really matter what the answer is or whether it's even possible to answer the question.
cues.zh: 其實答案是什麼，甚至能不能回答，都不太重要。

cues.en: Math is still really, really super duper, a lot useful regardless of where it comes from.
cues.zh: 不管從哪裡來，數學仍然非常、非常有用。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: Anyway, what I'm going to do now is describe the major positions on this debate that people take.
cues.zh: 總之，現在我要描述人們對這個辯論採取的主要立場。

cues.en: Now, there are generally four positions or four families that people fall into four camps.
cues.zh: 大致有四種立場、四個家族，也就是四個陣營。

cues.en: Let me start with the invented camp.
cues.zh: 先從「發明」陣營開始。

cues.en: So this approach claims that math is not a fundamental law of nature.
cues.zh: 這個觀點認為，數學不是根本的自然法則。

cues.en: Nature just exists the way it does.
cues.zh: 大自然就是以它原本的方式存在。

cues.en: So nature itself is fundamental to the texture of the universe, not mathematics.
cues.zh: 所以宇宙結構中根本的是大自然本身，不是數學。

cues.en: Instead, mathematics is a language that we humans have developed in order to build models of nature, to understand and characterize nature.
cues.zh: 數學反而是人類發展的語言，用來建立自然模型，理解並描述自然。

cues.en: And what are those models?
cues.zh: 那那些模型是什麼？

cues.en: What is mathematics?
cues.zh: 數學是什麼？

cues.en: Well, it's a set of rules, objects and relations between those objects.
cues.zh: 就是一組規則、物件，以及物件間的關係。

cues.en: And in the sense it's like other rules that we humans have invented, like board games and sports and laws and so on.
cues.zh: 這個意義上，和其他人類發明的規則類似，例如桌遊、運動、法律等等。

cues.en: And math is more precise than laws about like regulating the fossil fuel industry.
cues.zh: 數學比例如規範化石燃料產業的法律更精確，

cues.en: But it's the same concept.
cues.zh: 但概念相同。

cues.en: We have laws to describe and prescribe how humans can and should behave in different situations.
cues.zh: 我們有法律，描述、規範人類在不同情況下，可以與應該如何行動。

cues.en: And we have mathematics to describe how other things in nature can and should behave.
cues.zh: 也有數學，描述自然界其他事物可以與應該如何運作。

cues.en: And so people on this side of the debate will argue that the reason why math seems like it's so fundamental
cues.zh: 這一派會主張，數學看起來如此根本的原因，

cues.en: is that there's a huge space of mathematics millions, millions of equations, mathematical structures
cues.zh: 是數學有極大的空間，有幾百萬、幾百萬個方程式、數學結構

cues.en: and relations that people have invented, people have developed, and the vast majority of all of those
cues.zh: 與關係，都是人們發明、發展出來的，而這些數學

cues.en: possibilities in mathematics are completely, utterly useless in terms of understanding and describing nature.
cues.zh: 可能性，絕大多數對理解與描述自然，都完全沒用。

cues.en: But a tiny, tiny amount of invented math has turned out to be really accurate.
cues.zh: 只有極少數發明的數學，最後顯得非常準確。

cues.en: And people just talk about those small number of successes and ignore the majority of the math.
cues.zh: 人們只談少數成功案例，忽略大部分數學，

cues.en: That either isn't very accurate for describing nature or just isn't very relevant for describing nature.
cues.zh: 那些對描述自然不太準確，或沒太大關聯的數學。

cues.en: Okay, so math is invented.
cues.zh: 好，這是數學被發明的觀點。

cues.en: Then we have the camp of math is discovered.
cues.zh: 接著是數學被發現的陣營。

cues.en: These people will argue that math is fundamental to the universe.
cues.zh: 這些人主張，數學是宇宙的根本。

cues.en: Math is a set of structures and relations that are fundamental to nature, just as fundamental as gravity
cues.zh: 數學是一組自然中根本的結構與關係，就和重力、

cues.en: and electromagnetism, hydrogen atoms and so on.
cues.zh: 電磁作用、氫原子等等，一樣根本。

cues.en: And therefore, these people will also argue that intelligence is such as humans will eventually discover
cues.zh: 因此，他們也主張，人類這類智慧生命，終究會發現

cues.en: math the same way that we have discovered gravity and evolution by natural selection and other laws of nature.
cues.zh: 數學，就像我們發現重力、天擇演化，以及其他自然法則。

cues.en: And yeah.
cues.zh: 對。

cues.en: Now, here some people also go down religious or metaphysical arguments like claiming that math is the language of God.
cues.zh: 有些人也會走向宗教或形上學論述，例如宣稱數學是上帝的語言。

cues.en: Anyway, these are two dominant positions and they're both kind of extreme, right?
cues.zh: 總之，這是兩大主要立場，都有點極端，對吧？

cues.en: There's something in the middle, which is to say that there are some principles in math that are discovered and many other principles that are invented.
cues.zh: 還有介於中間的立場，認為有些數學原理是發現的，很多其他原理則是發明的。

cues.en: So there are certainly plenty of things in mathematics that have a weak or no relation to anything in nature.
cues.zh: 數學裡確實有很多東西，和大自然的任何事物關係很弱，或毫無關係。

cues.en: And of course, you see this a lot when you're studying calculus, because US instructors just make
cues.zh: 學微積分時經常看到，因為我們老師只為了

cues.en: up equations and formulas solely because they're useful for practicing like the chain rule, for example, without even a single thought as to whether that equation actually means anything.
cues.zh: 練習，例如鏈鎖律，就編出方程式與公式，完全不考慮它們是否真的代表什麼。

cues.en: So by analogy for this position, you can think about plastic, for example.
cues.zh: 可以用塑膠來類比這個立場。

cues.en: Plastic is a manmade material.
cues.zh: 塑膠是人造材料。

cues.en: You know, plastic water bottles don't exist in nature, not here on earth anyway.
cues.zh: 塑膠水瓶不會出現在自然界，至少地球上不會。

cues.en: Plastic water bottles don't grow on trees.
cues.zh: 不會長在樹上。

cues.en: So humans have invented plastic, but plastic is made from elementary elements like carbon and hydrogen.
cues.zh: 所以人類發明了塑膠，但它由碳、氫這類基本元素構成。

cues.en: And those elements were discovered by humans, not invented.
cues.zh: 這些元素則是人類發現的，不是發明的。

cues.en: So along these lines, an interesting thought experiment is what would happen if we ever meet some intelligent alien species and compared our math textbooks to theirs.
cues.zh: 沿著這個思路，一個有趣的思想實驗是，如果有一天遇到智慧外星物種，把我們的數學教科書和他們的比較，會怎樣？

cues.en: And this intermediate position would basically claim that we'd have some overlap with alien math, but mostly a lot of unique math that we invented.
cues.zh: 中間立場基本上會認為，我們和外星數學有些重疊，但主要是很多我們發明、

cues.en: And they didn't and vice versa.
cues.zh: 他們沒發明的獨特數學，反過來也一樣。

cues.en: And you know, you can think about a number fields like integers, rational and irrational numbers, maybe those types of structures are universal.
cues.zh: 可以想像，整數、有理數、無理數這些數域，也許這類結構是普世的。

cues.en: And then we have something like matrix multiplication and perhaps that was invented and cultural.
cues.zh: 然後有矩陣乘法這種東西，也許是發明的、文化性的。

cues.en: Then we have the final position here.
cues.zh: 最後一個立場。

cues.en: Now this may seem like it's not an actual intellectual position on a philosophical debate, and instead it's just a lazy excuse to disengage from the discussion.
cues.zh: 看起來可能不像哲學辯論中真正的思想立場，反而像懶得參與討論的藉口。

cues.en: But this is actually a valid position of the argument, and it's focused on these successes of math
cues.zh: 但這其實是個有效的立場，著重於數學的成功，

cues.en: and the amazing improvements in human life and society that have come directly from applications of mathematics.
cues.zh: 以及數學應用直接帶給人類生活與社會的驚人改善。

cues.en: Now, you know, here I like to think of an analogy of airplanes and birds.
cues.zh: 我喜歡用飛機與鳥類來比喻。

cues.en: Airplanes are not the same thing as birds.
cues.zh: 飛機和鳥不是同一回事。

cues.en: I mean, they both fly, they both have wings.
cues.zh: 都會飛，都有翅膀。

cues.en: But what a crazy thing to spend time debating whether airplanes are like birds.
cues.zh: 但花時間辯論飛機像不像鳥，真是件奇怪的事，

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: Airplanes have an unquantifiable huge impact on modern life.
cues.zh: 飛機對現代生活有難以量化的巨大影響。

cues.en: And the question of whether airplanes and birds are similar is it's just totally senseless.
cues.zh: 而飛機與鳥是否相似，這個問題根本毫無意義。

cues.en: It's such a waste of time.
cues.zh: 太浪費時間。

cues.en: Likewise, the argument here is that even having this debate about whether math is discovered or invented is a waste of intellectual energy.
cues.zh: 同樣地，這裡的主張是，就連辯論數學是發現還是發明，都在浪費思考的精力。

cues.en: Imagine what people could accomplish if they were using mathematics and developing mathematics for important
cues.zh: 想像大家不花時間辯論，而把數學用於、發展於能幫助

cues.en: applications that would help humans and human society instead of spending time having this debate.
cues.zh: 人類與人類社會的重要應用，可以成就多少事情。

cues.en: So enough with the distraction and let's get back to actually using math to make the world a better place.
cues.zh: 所以別再分心，回去真正用數學，讓世界更美好。

cues.en: That is the position of this argument anyway.
cues.zh: 總之，這就是這個論點的立場。

cues.en: So those are the major.
cues.zh: 這些就是主要的立場，

cues.en: On this discussion.
cues.zh: 關於這個討論的立場。

cues.en: This is the same slide from the beginning of the lecture.
cues.zh: 這是課程一開始的同一張投影片。

cues.en: Now, if you find this discussion interesting, then I encourage you to spend some time looking up online.
cues.zh: 如果覺得有趣，鼓勵你花時間上網查。

cues.en: Lots and lots of websites, YouTube videos, podcasts you can find, including some interviews with some of the greatest mathematicians and physicists of the 20th century.
cues.zh: 有很多網站、YouTube 影片、Podcast，包括對二十世紀一些最偉大數學家與物理學家的訪談。

cues.en: And of course, if you're not really interested in this discussion, then I hope you at least found this short overview of the debate to be interesting and worth your time.
cues.zh: 當然，如果你不太感興趣，希望至少覺得這個簡短的辯論概述，有趣而值得花時間。

cues.en: Either way, it is now time to transition from the basic calculus you learned in the previous sections to the next level of calculus understanding, which we will start in the next section.
cues.zh: 不管如何，現在該從前幾節的基礎微積分，轉向下一層次的理解，下一節就開始。
